title: Climates of the World
seo_title: Grade 3 Climate Worksheets: Weather vs. Climate and Climates of Different Regions
standard_text: Obtain and combine information to describe climates in different regions of the world.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on climate (NGSS 3-ESS2-2): weather vs. climate, tropical, desert, polar, temperate and mountain climates, and comparing city climate data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Climate is the usual weather of a place over many years.
key_sub: Tropical places are hot and rainy, deserts are dry, polar places are cold, and temperate places have four seasons.
body_html:
How to think about it

Weather is what the air is like on one day. Climate is the usual weather in a place over many years.

  • Tropical: hot and rainy all year (rain forests, Hawaii).
  • Desert: very dry (Phoenix, the Sahara).
  • Polar: very cold all year (Antarctica, northern Alaska).
  • Temperate: four seasons (Chicago, New York).
  • Mountain: cooler and windier higher up.

Places near the equator are warm; places near the poles are cold. We learn a place's climate from many years of weather data.

Example

“It is snowing in Denver today.” Weather or climate?

It is about one day.

Answer: weather

Example

A city gets 150 mm of rain a year. What climate is it?

Very little rain.

Answer: desert

Common mistakes

  • Thinking one day's weather tells you the climate.
  • Thinking all deserts are hot. Deserts are dry.
  • Thinking places near the equator have cold winters.

faq.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
faq.a: Weather is what the air is like on one day. Climate is the usual weather pattern over many years.

faq.q: What are the main kinds of climate?
faq.a: Tropical (hot and rainy), desert (very dry), polar (very cold), temperate (four seasons) and mountain (cooler higher up).
No. A desert is a place with very little rain. Antarctica is a cold desert.

items.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
c: Weather is what happens on one day; climate is the usual pattern over many years.
items.e: Weather is short-term; climate is long-term.

items.q: Why do scientists study climate?
c: to know what weather a place usually has so people can plan
items.e: Climate helps people choose crops, clothes and buildings.

items.q: Ava reads this sentence: “It is raining in Chicago this afternoon.” Is it about weather or climate?

items.e: It tells what is happening at one time, so it is weather.

items.q: Are all deserts hot?
